title: Safe Deposit Boxes: Surrendering a Box and Moving to Another Size
content:
A lessee of Safe Deposit Boxes may give a box up for good, or trade it for a different size at the same branch. Both paths return part of the rent already paid; this page defines how much, and what must be true of the rental's balance.

## Settings by box size

| Box size | Unused whole months refunded on surrender | First rental year's rent refundable | Unused months credited on a size move |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3x5 Safe Deposit Box | Yes | No | Yes |
| 3x10 Safe Deposit Box | Yes | No | Yes |
| 5x10 Safe Deposit Box | Yes | No | Yes |
| 10x10 Safe Deposit Box | Yes | No | Yes |
| 10x15 Safe Deposit Box | Yes | No | Yes |
| 10x20 Safe Deposit Box | Yes | No | Yes |

## The rental's balance

What a lessee owes on a single box rental is the rent, late fees and service fees charged to it, reduced by the payments and credits applied to it. A figure below zero means the bank owes the lessee that credit.

A box can be surrendered, or exchanged for another size, only when that balance shows nothing outstanding, meaning it stands at zero or in the lessee's favour. The bank's record of the rental's balance is what counts, not the lessee's statement that it has been settled.

## Giving up a box

Surrender is a decision for the lessee alone. The lessee comes to the branch personally, clears everything out of the box and hands back its keys, and the rental is then closed.

**Unused rent.** For every size, unused whole months of paid rent are refunded. Those months are the full calendar months that remain after the month in which the surrender falls, running up to the end of the most recent rental year that has been both charged and paid. Each such month is credited at a monthly rate equal to that year's net rent divided by the number of months in the rental term, rounded half-up to the cent. Rent belonging to the first rental year of the lease is never refunded, for any size.

**Key deposit.** The key deposit is credited back only if every key that was issued comes back. If any key is not returned, the deposit is not credited and the lock-change fee is charged in its place.

**Paying out a credit.** Where these credits leave the rental in credit, the balance is paid either into a PCB checking account belonging to the lessee or by official check.

### Hypothetical illustrations

| Hypothetical facts | Result |
|---|---|
| Second rental year runs 1 February to 31 January, charged and paid; monthly rate works out at 10.00; surrender on 20 June; all keys returned | July through January are 7 whole months, so 70.00 of rent is credited, and the key deposit is credited back |
| Same year, surrender on 25 January | No whole month remains after January, so no rent is credited |
| Surrender in the fifth month of the lease's first rental year, no later year paid | No rent is credited, since first-year rent is never refunded |
| Surrender with one key missing | The key deposit is not credited, and the lock-change fee is charged |

## Moving to a different size

A lessee may switch the rental to a different box size within the same branch's vault. The rental keeps its anniversary, so its rent due date does not shift. For every size, the rent already paid on the box being left is credited for its unused whole months; for that same span of months the lessee is charged the net rent of the box being taken up; and the size-change fee is applied.
